top_findings.title: MCP server registration is broken and has no working entrypoint
top_findings.evidence: mcp_server.py:831-832 runs `mcp_server.tool()(tool)` at module import against `Server` from mcp.server (the low-level SDK Server); that class has no `.tool()` method — only `list_tools()`/`call_tool()`/`run()` decorators (confirmed in installed mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py:440,498,646), so the import raises AttributeError. `handle_tool` (mcp_server.py:770) is never wired via @call_tool, get_tools() is never wired via @list_tools, and there is no stdio entrypoint / mcp_server.run() / __main__. Tool definitions (get_tools, mcp_server.py:670) and a dispatch handler exist, but the server cannot run.
top_findings.suggestion: Register with `@mcp_server.list_tools()` returning get_tools() and `@mcp_server.call_tool()` delegating to handle_tool, then add an async main using mcp.server.stdio.stdio_server() + mcp_server.run(); guard with `if __name__ == "__main__"`.
